problem: Prior outdoor VLN work (Touchdown) only evaluated on seen areas where test routes lie in the same region as training routes, so generalization to unseen outdoor areas and the real role of visual input were unknown.
motivation: Indoor VLN shows sharp performance drops in unseen environments, but outdoor VLN had not been tested that way. The authors want to know which representations (graph features, images, instruction tokens) drive success in unseen areas, and whether current outdoor VLN is biased toward artifacts of the urban graph.
key_idea: Introduce an unseen-area outdoor VLN split and a simple ORAR seq2seq agent with graph-derived junction type embedding and heading delta features, then show that these features, not images, drive most unseen-area gains.
insight: Removing the junction type embedding collapses unseen TC (e.g. Touchdown 14.9 to 4.3, map2seq 30.3 to 7.1), and a no-image model matches image models on map2seq unseen (30.5 vs 30.3), so gains come from graph-specific features rather than visual grounding. Oracle sub-task analysis shows low-level ResNet features mostly help the orientation sub-task, and doubling training data with merged datasets does not help the no-image model, so the bottleneck is the amount of panorama/area diversity, not the number of instructions.
method: ORAR model: seq2seq agent with a BiLSTM instruction encoder and a two-layer LSTM decoder (observation recurrence, then attention recurrence), where multi-head attention over text is followed by attention over panorama slices

Visual encoder: panorama sliced into 8 views with 60° FOV, 5 fed to ResNet; variants are ResNet-18 4th-to-last low-level features (100x100), ResNet-50 pre-final (5x2048), semantic segmentation (25-class Mapillary area vector), or no image
Junction type embedding: embeds the number of outgoing edges of the current node, categorized into {2,3,4,>4}, so the agent can recognise intersections
Heading delta: normalized (-1,1] heading change relative to the previous step, which corrects for the environment's automatic rotation toward the closest outgoing edge
Unseen split: geographic boundary across lower Manhattan separates train and dev/test areas, with boundary-crossing routes discarded; map2seq is adapted to VLN and merged with Touchdown

Analyses: sub-task oracles (orientation/directions/stopping), object vs direction token masking during train and test, architecture ablations, and a mixed model using different visual features for the first action

setting.backbone: ORAR: BiLSTM text encoder + 2-layer LSTM decoder with multi-head attention, ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18/ResNet-50 image features (trained from scratch apart from the frozen ResNet)
setting.model_size: small (256-d LSTMs, 32-d BPE embeddings); ~3 h training on one GTX 1080 Ti
setting.training_data: Touchdown (9,326 routes) and map2seq (7,672 instructions), separately or merged, on Manhattan street-view graph (29,641 panoramas); seen and unseen splits
setting.observation: street-view panorama (sliced views or semantic segmentation), plus junction type and heading delta from the graph
setting.action_space: discrete graph actions: forward, left, right, stop
setting.simulator: Touchdown Manhattan street-view panorama graph environment
setting.privileged: none (junction type is derivable by rotating in place, but uses graph structure)

results: ORAR significantly outperforms RConcat, GA, ARC and VLN Transformer on seen Touchdown (TC 29.1 vs 16.7 for ARC+l2s) and map2seq. In the unseen scenario it reaches TC 14.9 on Touchdown and 30.3 on map2seq, versus at most 3.1 and 3.5 for the baselines, and most of the gain depends on junction type. Merging datasets improves results, and images add little in unseen areas.
limitations: Only a single small Manhattan area with a geographic split, so conclusions about generalization may not extend to more diverse cities
Features such as junction type and heading delta are graph-specific and would not transfer to continuous environments
Simple LSTM architecture with no large-scale pretraining; absolute unseen performance remains low (TC 15 on Touchdown)
